targets.classification: codec / contract with excessive imported capability
targets.reason: Review repository needs verdict schema only; the same module imports authoring validation and Node crypto through definition hashing.
targets.deletionCondition: Separate review-record schemas from review identity operations; repository schema import no longer reaches authoring validation or crypto.

primitives.owner: workflows/primitives: shared AgentCall, lane, artifact, gate and envelope modules
primitives.deletionCondition: None while the supported primitive serves graph and its other consumers. Retire a primitive only through the adoption matrix; do not duplicate its decisions in graph.

primitive-composition.owner: graph production/lane tool composition, using workflow primitive stores
primitive-composition.deletionCondition: Remove from a caller if that caller becomes a pure core; supply the store/service via its declared port then.

conversation-contract.owner: conversation lifecycle semantic manager and turn contracts
conversation-contract.deletionCondition: None while graph turns run as conversations. Consumers use semantic admission, cancellation and result contracts, never raw actor events.

conversation-adapter.deletionCondition: Remove only when the graph operation no longer uses the conversation-hosted execution shape; do not bypass its transcript/cancellation ownership.

conversation-composition.owner: conversation production binding of graph-provided runtime instructions/result delivery
conversation-composition.disposition: retain only in the production boundary
conversation-composition.deletionCondition: Any occurrence in a designated lifecycle core must move behind an injected hook. Production bindings remain explicit while those graph features exist.

graph-authoring-contract.owner: graph authoring semantics, persisted definitions and diagnostic vocabulary
graph-authoring-contract.deletionCondition: No edge-count deletion target. Consolidate ownership only if the authoring API itself changes; migrate historical decoders only after retained rows no longer need them.

graph-authoring-adapter.owner: graph definition/template HTTP and validation adapters (currently split across workflows and workflow-graph)
graph-authoring-adapter.deletionCondition: Move or delete only with a responsibility-based authoring-adapter consolidation. Graph engine and generic primitives must not acquire HTTP response construction.

graph-authoring-composition.deletionCondition: Remove if a caller is extracted into a pure authoring core; bind the same service/port at the outer route instead.

graph-merge-adapter.owner: merge lifecycle; graph-merge-runner adapts graph joins to the supported merge machine
graph-merge-adapter.deletionCondition: None merely because it imports the machine. Replace only if a semantic merge-host API subsumes both graph and job hosting without duplicating phase/outcome logic.

graph-merge-policy.owner: graph lifecycle owns execution lease; merge initiation/publish consume its admission decision
graph-merge-policy.deletionCondition: None while graph lease governs session delivery. Keep the authoritative publish check under its lock even when an advisory preflight exists.

collaboration-contract.owner: collaboration protocol and graph collaboration configuration
collaboration-contract.deletionCondition: Split neutral artifact vocabulary from graph configuration only if independent change or broader reuse requires it; preserve one artifact shape and frozen config decoding.

collaboration-adapter.owner: collaboration slice; graph collaborator caller adapts graph lanes to its artifacts/prompts/policy
collaboration-adapter.disposition: supported composition of a collaboration slice
collaboration-adapter.deletionCondition: None while graph invokes this slice. Do not create a second negotiator to remove cross-folder edges.

collaboration-composition.owner: graph lane-tool production loader binding the collaboration slice
collaboration-composition.deletionCondition: Move behind injected collaborators if lane-tool core is separated; production agent callers/stores must remain outside that core.

workflow-composition.owner: workflows/production.ts composition shared by graph and merge hosts; graph/merge own the declared ports
workflow-composition.deletionCondition: No deletion target while both hosts share these bindings. Pure engines must receive the resulting ports rather than import this root.

live-read-contract.owner: graph lifecycle/result/event vocabularies; workflow queries and SSE reactions are client adapters
live-read-contract.deletionCondition: None while UI and transport consume those graph records. Do not infer a runtime policy violation from a type-only import.

review-identity.owner: graph plan review identity; graph owns canonical definition hashing
review-identity.disposition: retain canonical hash; separate it from review-record schema loading
review-identity.deletionCondition: The review repository schema import must no longer reach plan validation or Node crypto. Keep canonical authored-field selection and resulting hashes identical.
